{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that face emotional valence perception would decrease with increasing eccentricity, and that eccentricity might have different effects on different emotional valences due to potentially dissociated underlying mechanisms.",
  "design": "mixed, with eccentricity (0°, 2°, 4°) and emotional valence (positive, neutral, negative) as within-participant factors.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "The eccentricity of the facial stimuli (0°, 2°, or 4° from the center of the visual field) and the emotional valence of the faces (positive, neutral, or negative).",
  "outcome_measure": "Categorization accuracy and response time for identifying the emotional valence of the faces.",
  "population_and_setting": "Adults with normal or corrected-to-normal vision, tested in a laboratory setting using an eye-tracking system to monitor fixation.",
  "sample_size_total": 56,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Participants were recruited and reimbursed for their efforts; the study was approved by the Bar Ilan University ethics committee.",
  "analysis_plan": "Two-way repeated-measures ANOVAs (eccentricity x valence) for accuracy and reaction times, followed by post-hoc analyses with Bonferroni adjustment.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used two experimental designs: a block-design (where participants reported the dominant valence of a sequence) and a single-trial design (where participants reported the valence of each individual stimulus). Stimuli were 2° x 2.71° grayscale portraits presented for 200 ms. Fixation was monitored and trials with gaze shifts >1° were excluded."
